claims.statement: Zendesk documents API tokens as auto-generated passwords created in Admin Center (Apps and integrations > APIs > Zendesk API), sent as Basic authentication credentials in the form {email_address}/token:{api_token}; the email address and the literal /token separator are part of the credential string, the token is the secret part.

sources.supports: API tokens are auto-generated passwords in the Zendesk Admin Center. ... Basic authentication is used for API tokens. ... Use the following format for the credentials: {email_address}/token:{api_token}

claims.statement: Zendesk documents that Support API tokens are being retired in three phases: from 2026-07-28 tokens unused for 30 days are deactivated (and deleted after 60 further days) and new accounts cannot create or use them; from 2026-10-27 existing accounts cannot create new tokens; on 2027-04-30 all remaining tokens are permanently deactivated. The pages call the API token deprecated and say existing customers must migrate to OAuth access tokens.

sources.supports: Zendesk API tokens will be permanently deactivated on April 30, 2027. ... Zendesk is retiring Support API tokens in three phases between July 2026 and April 2027.

If you're an existing Zendesk customer and are currently using basic authentication or API tokens, you will have to migrate to OAuth access tokens for improved security and compatibility with future requirements.

claims.statement: Two open-source scanner rule artifacts by different maintainers both treat the Zendesk API token as a run of exactly 40 characters from a letters-and-digits alphabet that follows the keyword zendesk (the TruffleHog artifact also admits underscore and hyphen). This records consistency between those artifacts only; it is not Zendesk's stated format, and the provider pages read give no length or alphabet for API tokens.

sources.supports: Rule zendesk-secret-key (keyword zendesk) captures ([a-z0-9]{40}) after an assignment-style separator, case-insensitive.

The token pattern is the keyword zendesk followed by ([A-Za-z0-9_-]{40}); the detector sends the token as Basic auth with the username email plus /token, matching the documented credential composition.

openQuestions.question: The provider pages read state no length or alphabet for the API token; the only support for a 40-character letters-and-digits shape is the tool-corroborated claim, which is consistency between two scanner rule artifacts and not a provider statement (the provider's one example value happens to be 40 characters but is not declared representative). A bare value must not be attributed to Zendesk from shape alone; the documented context is the {email_address}/token:{api_token} Basic credential.

Whether detection evidence should treat the email address and the token as separate identifier and secret parts of one Basic credential string is a modelling question for research-family; this record only states the documented composition.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.
Whether older or newer API tokens differ in length or alphabet is not established by either artifact or by the provider pages.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Candidate existence established from Zendesk developer documentation read on 2026-10-04; the family is not researched beyond what the claims state.
